51610794.protein: Nuclear receptor subfamily 2 group E member 1
51610794.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human TLX LBD assessed as dissociation constant by ITC analysis
51610794.references_previous: Reference 20: Faudon, G.; Kilu, W.; Ni, X.; Chaikaud, A.; Sreeramulu, S.; Heitel, P.; Schwalbe, H.; Knapp, S.; Schubert-Zsilavecz, M.; Heering, J.; Merk, D. The Transcriptional Repressor Orphan Nuclear Receptor TLX Is Responsive to Xanthines. ACS Pharmacol. Transl. Sci. 2021, 4 (6), 1794–1807.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Isothermal Titration Calorimetry (ITC) experiments were conducted on an Affinity ITC instrument (TA Instruments, New Castle, DE) at 25 °C with a stirring rate of 75 rpm. The TLX LBD protein (10–20 μM, expressed as described previously20) in buffer (20 mM Tris pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 0.2 mM TCEP, 5% glycerol) containing 1–4% DMSO was titrated with the test compounds (60–100 μM in the same buffer containing 1–4% DMSO) in 26 injections (1 × 1 μL, 25 × 4 μL) with an injection interval of 150 s. As control experiments, the test compounds were titrated to the buffer, and the buffer was titrated to the TLX LBD protein under otherwise identical conditions. Results were analyzed using NanoAnalyze software (version 3.11.0, TA Instruments, New Castle, DE) with independent binding models.
original_paragraph.Figure 1 caption: Figure 1. Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) orthogonally validated binding of 31 (a) and 34 (b) to the human TLX LBD. The fittings of the heat of binding are shown and the isotherms at 25 °C are shown as insets.

Data are the mean ± S.E.M., n ≥ 3. All compounds were counterscreened to exclude nonspecific effects on VP16 activity. bKd values from ITC (Figures 1 and S2).
